name: Unthlatu
body:
UNTHLATU
CR 1

This reptilian human has smooth, glossy scales of mottled green and brown and clever eyes above its fanged mouth.

XP 400
N Medium humanoid
Init +2

DEFENSE

AC 12, touch 12, flat-footed 10 (+2 Dex)
hp 15 (2d8+6)
Fort +3, Ref +5, Will +0
Defensive Abilities slip away; Immune pinned

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee bite +2 (1d6+1 plus unthlatu venom 1/day), shortspear +2 (1d6+1)
Special Attacks unthlatu venom

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 14, Con 16, Int 11, Wis 11, Cha 11
Base Atk +1; CMB +3; CMD 14
Feats Agile Maneuvers
Skills Escape Artist +4, Stealth +4
Languages Common, Unthlatu

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Unthlatu Venom (Ex)

Bite-injury save Fortitude DC 14; frequency 1/minute for 10 minutes; cure 2 saves. The victim is sickened for 1 minute. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Slip Away (Ex)

An unthlatu has +2 on Escape Artist checks to end a grapple and may do so as a swift action instead of a standard action.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, patrol (2-4), or village (10+)
Treasure standard

The Unthlatu are reclusive humanoids who generally keep to themselves. They are completely hairless and have scales covering their entire body with patterns resembling a python or boa, while their eyes are similar to a serpents, having green or yellow scelera and vertical slits for pupils.

In combat, unthlatu are difficult to pin down because of their serpentine anatomies, able to slip away from grapples and snares due to the combination of their incredibly smooth scales and articulated flexibility. In addition, they are venomous, able to sicken opponents with their bite.

Because of their reclusive nature, unthlatu and their customs are relatively unknown. Like some fey creatures, they seem to follow their own code of conduct, which causes friction while dealing with outsiders. One day they will steal cattle from a neighboring settlement, while the next they will come to aid the same village with tools and supplies. This is further compounded by them having their own language which is difficult to learn. However, outsiders who take the time to learn their language will be treated with respect for their efforts.
